name: Badeucy
description: Badeucy is a sophisticated split-pot poker variant that blends the mechanics of Badugi with Deuce-to-Seven Triple Draw. In this high-stakes favorite, players aim to build two specific low hands: a 4-card 'Badugi' (four different suits and ranks) and a 5-card Deuce-to-Seven low. Unlike its sister game Badacey, Aces in Badeucy are always high and detrimental, making the 2-3-4-5-7 'Wheel' the ultimate goal.

history.origins: Part of the modern 'Mixed Game' evolution in high-stakes poker rooms. It was popularized by players who enjoyed the complexity of Deuce-to-Seven Lowball and wanted to add a Badugi component back when Badugi was the newest trend in the mid-2000s.
timeline: Mid-2000s: Emerges in California 'Big Game' mixes.
2010s: Becomes a standard rotation in WSOP 'Dealer's Choice' and 'Mixed Triple Draw' events.
Present: Highly regarded as one of the most strategically deep draw games in professional poker.
history.cultural: Regarded as a game where 'every card counts', demanding extreme discipline in starting hand selection.
history.evolution: Badeucy is considered more 'pure' than Badacey by many experts because the Ace-high constraint makes hand-building significantly more difficultâ€”you cannot use the Ace for your Lowball half.

setup.players: Two to six players. All players make an ante bet; the dealer gives each player five cards face down, then a round of betting and three draw-and-bet cycles before the final betting and split-pot showdown.
setup.dealing: 5 cards face down to each player. 3 draw phases follow.
setup.equipment: Poker chips, Dealer button, Small/Big Blind markers.

rules.objective: Win half the pot with the best 4-card Badugi and half with the best 5-card Deuce-to-Seven low.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Blinds**: Initial stakes. 2. **Deal**: 5 cards. 3. **Betting**. 4. **Three Draws**: Discard/draw rounds punctuated by betting. 5. **Showdown**: Split resolution.
keyRules: Aces count as high (above Kings) and are essentially useless in a winning hand.
Straights and Flushes are active: if you hold 2-3-4-5-6 of mixed suits, you have a straight (bad for low), but you have a 4-card Badugi (2-3-4-5).
If you hold five hearts, your Lowball half is a Flush and will lose to almost any non-flush hand.

strategy.basic: Avoid the Ace. In Badeucy, the Ace is a 'dead card' for your low hand. If you start with an Ace, discard it immediately unless it's part of a desperate Badugi bluff.
strategy.intermediate: Manage suits carefully. Unlike Badacey where flushes don't matter, in Badeucy you must ACTIVELY AVOID flushes for your Lowball half. This means your 4-card Badugi (mixed suits) is naturally aligned with a good Lowball hand.
strategy.advanced: Range Polarization: Because straights and flushes are 'bad', you can tell a lot about an opponent's hand by how many cards they draw. Specifically, a player drawing zero cards ('Standing Pat') is very likely to have a 7-low or 8-low that is NOT a straight.
tips: The 'Hammer': A hand like 2-3-4-5-7 rainbow is the ultimate weapon in this game.
If you have four cards to a wheel (2-3-4-5), but two are the same suit, your Badugi is technically only 3 cards (2-3-4). This is a 'Rough' hand; don't overplay it.

variations.name: Badacey

scoring.winCondition: Lowest 5-card low (A high) + Lowest 4-card Badugi (A high).
